nodes.question: How do non-cooperative taxes and subsidies compare to first-best policies?
nodes.answer: Non-cooperative taxes are lower, while non-cooperative subsidies are higher compared to first-best policies.
nodes.paragraph: Abstract Using a general equilibrium model of symmetric countries, this paper analyzes a non-cooperative game in environmental policies under transboundary pollution. Emission taxes on polluting firms and subsidies to environmental firms are available policy instruments. Environmental firms which produce pollution abatement goods and services engage in imperfect competition. Mobile capital is employed in each country by polluting and environmental firms. Compared with the first-best poli-cies, non-cooperative taxes are lower, whereas non-cooperative subsidies are higher. Although excessive subsidies mitigate the distortionary effect of inefficiently low emission taxes, the equilibrium level of pollution is inefficiently high due to overin- vestment in polluting firms and underinvestment in environmental firms. This ana- lytical result suggests that there are limitations to what non-cooperative tax and sub- sidy policies can achieve regarding transboundary pollution. Keywords Taxes Subsidies Imperfect competition Transboundary pollution Capital mobility JEL Classification F12 H23 Q58 1 Introduction Polluting firms engage in pollution management (e.g., air and water pollution abate- ments) to abide by environmental policies and regulations. Environmental goods (e.g., filtering apparatus for gases and water purification machines) are often pro- vided by specialized private firms.

nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is the impact of high environmental subsidies according to the paper?
nodes.answer: High environmental subsidies mitigate the distortion of low taxes but lead to an inefficiently high equilibrium level of pollution.
nodes.paragraph: 2008; David et al. 2011). Environmental Economics and Policy Studies with local pollution, Canton (2007), Greaker and Rosendahl (2008), Nimubona (2012), and Sugiyama et al. (2023) analyze in detail the effects of environmental policies on the terms of trade, cross-border profit shifting, and imperfect competi- tion.6 Although Fischer et al. (2017, 2018) consider the case of transboundary pollu- tion, their analyses are limited to environmental subsidies under exogenous taxes or regulations. In studies on environmental industries and multiple policy instruments, when examining the welfare effects of one instrument, other instruments are often assumed to be exogenous.7 In this paper, the simultaneous choice of tax and subsidy policies is considered. This paper shows that, under transboundary pollution, non-cooperative emission taxes are lower than the Pigouvian level, whereas non-cooperative environmental subsidies are higher than the efficient level under imperfect competition. Although high subsidies mitigate the distortion of low taxes to some extent, the equilibrium level of pollution is inefficiently high. Thus, transboundary pollution reduces the effectiveness of environmental policies under non-cooperative policymaking.

nodes.question: What is the main focus of the paper regarding public policy finance for energy subsidies?
nodes.answer: The paper evaluates common methods of energy subsidy cost-recovery, specifically a flat-rate household levy and an electricity price surcharge, considering both equity and efficiency effects.
nodes.paragraph: We nd that while ef ciency grows in relative importance as the magnitude of the subsidycost increases, equity still outweighs the ef ciency loss in many circumstances given likelysocietal preferences for inequality. Should policy costs be negative, a at-rate levy is welfare-maximising under all conditions.
